subject: Configurable locality + per-tenant purge scheduling — FinHealth requirements
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura@finhealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: FinHealth Legal <legal@finhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency + retention: FinHealth minimal asks

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — FinHealth leadership kicked off a short compliance checklist and we have a few hard requirements that will determine whether we can move to Redwood Dedicated for production: 

- Data locality: All PHI-adjacent transcripts and embeddings MUST be stored in the US (single region: us-west-2) for the first 12 months.
- Retention: Audit logs and transaction records need a 7-year retention for regulatory purposes; user-generated conversational logs should be configurable per workspace (from 30 days up to 7 years).
- Deletion: Support for immediate on-demand erasure of a tenant's conversational data (not just soft-delete) and an admin-initiated export prior to deletion.

Can you confirm whether these are configurable today or if they'll require roadmap work? We also attached a short retention matrix we use internally (finhealth-retention-mapping.csv).

Appreciate any clarity on timelines — our procurement deadline is end of October.

Best,
Laura
Director, Compliance
FinHealth

[Attachment: finhealth-retention-mapping.csv (csv)]

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@finhealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency + retention: FinHealth minimal asks

Laura — thanks for the clear checklist and the CSV, that's super helpful. Short answers up-front:

- Data locality: hosted Redwood currently supports region pinning for customer workloads in our hosted + dedicated flows, but we don't yet expose a per-tenant UI toggle that guarantees "single-region at rest and compute" semantics in our self-serve console.
- Retention config: we have default retention config, and soft-delete APIs exist today. We don't currently have an admin flow for on-demand permanent erasure plus pre-deletion export in a single self-serve action.
- Timeline: we can scope a prioritized roadmap item for per-tenant configurable retention + regional storage with an admin-safe permanent-erase + export action.

I've looped in Kar thik (serving/runtime) and Monica (product) to scope technical complexity and propose a pragmatic timeline that meets your procurement window if possible. Can you confirm whether the 7-year audit retention needs to be in the same US region or if cold-archival in a separate US region is acceptable? Also any specifics about KMS/HSM key separation would be helpful.

I'll follow up with a proposed plan and minimal-risk approach.

— Jasmine
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: FinHealth-SOC2-evidence.xlsx (xlsx) — reference only]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Chen <laura@finhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 11:05:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency + retention: FinHealth minimal asks

Thanks, Jasmine. Quick engineering read: 

1) Region enforcement: we currently pin compute and hot storage to regions for Dedicated pools, but audit logs flow into a central cold-store pipeline today. For strict single-region retention of audit logs, we'd need to add a per-tenant sink selector and route cold archives to a region-specific bucket. Work estimate: 3-4 sprints (with infra + storage + compliance review).

2) Per-tenant retention windows & admin-erase: the runtime already supports TTLs for in-memory caches and short-term stores. Making this robust for long-term archives and a guaranteed "hard delete" (with verifiable wipe) requires:
   - a tenant metadata flag and admin API (low complexity)
   - an export job that snapshots all tenant artifacts to an encrypted archive (medium complexity)
   - a background permanent-deletion pipeline that removes blob references and triggers key-rotation or rekeying for zero-access proofs (higher complexity; needs security sign-off)

3) UX: need an admin UI and audit trail for any on-demand erasure. That needs product + legal involvement.

Proposed options for FinHealth: 
A) Fast path (45 days): per-tenant region pinning for compute+hot store + admin export API; soft-delete remains the default, with COE runbook for legal requests.
B) Compliant path (3 months): A) + region-specific cold-archive routing + admin-initiated hard-delete with verifiable wipe and KMS key isolation.

Happy to break these into milestones and produce a dev plan.

— Karthik
Senior Staff Eng, Serving Runtime

From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Chen <laura@finhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 09:17:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency + retention: FinHealth minimal asks

Laura / team — thank you for the detail. Based on Karthik's breakdown I've sketched a proposal that meets both procurement timing and compliance needs. High level: 

- Sprint 1 (2 weeks): Deliver per-tenant region pinning for Dedicated instances (compute + hot store) and an admin-only export API to snapshot tenant data. Minimal QA + legal review.
- Sprint 2 (3 weeks): Implement region-targeted cold-archive routing and retention policy configuration in the admin console (UI + API).
- Sprint 3 (3 weeks): Hard-delete pipeline + key isolation and audit trail; include playbook for verified deletion and export evidence.

Target delivery for Compliant path (Option B from Karthik) = ~8 weeks from start. If FinHealth needs contractual guarantees in October, we can scope a SOC/contract addendum promising the roadmap and an interim SLA that includes manual verified deletion executed by our security operations team as a fallback.

Action items for FinHealth to help accelerate:
- Confirm whether cold-archival location must be the same AZ or simply the same region (us-west-2).
- Provide KMS key separation requirements (separate key per tenant or per-account key policy).
- Share any acceptance criteria for what constitutes a verifiable hard-delete (e.g., crypto shred proof, deletion receipts).

I'll draft this into a short MLP PRD and share the link.

— Monica
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

[Link: https://drive.google.com/finhealth-retention-specs]

3) FinHealth to confirm KMS and cold-archive region constraints by Monday 9/20 so we can finalize acceptance criteria.

Thanks — we'll treat this as high priority for the Dedicated pipeline.
